title: Change the fuse in an unplugged UK plug
instruction: Replace the fuse in the unplugged plug with the spare of the same rating, and refit its fuse carrier securely.
setup: A fully unplugged moulded UK plug, 54 x 45 mm, with three standard pins, a short inert cable, a removable 32 x 9 mm fuse carrier and passive spring clips. A marked old 25.4 x 6.3 mm BS1362 cartridge fuse is retained inside. One loose replacement of the same rating rests on an 18 x 18 x 12 mm wooden block. A 169 mm flat screwdriver with a 3 mm blade lies on two wooden rests. An 85 x 70 mm parts dish is beside them. Both grippers have 2 x 18 x 24 mm silicone pad covers. Start as pictured; no mains connection is present.
scoring: 1.0 if the old fuse is at least 4 cm outside its seat, the replacement has both metal ends in the terminal clips, the carrier is refitted flush and the parts stay retained for three seconds after release. 0.5 for removing the old fuse and seating the replacement without closing the carrier; 0.25 for removing the old fuse alone. Otherwise 0. Broken clips or housing, or parts dropped off the table, score 0. Inspect the clips and carrier in the video with a ruler; this is a mechanical replacement test, not an electrical test.
fidelity: The plug, cartridge fuses and screwdriver are rigid native bodies. Passive spring leaves and detents approximate terminal retention and the removable carrier. The robot must lever, grasp, align and press the parts through contact. Clip stiffness and failure loads are approximate. No electricity, fuse continuity or mains operation is simulated. Development validation is incomplete.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: Replacing a plug fuse combines opening a small retained cover with extracting, aligning and reseating a cartridge.
